statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-58045: a TypedArray whose length and byteLength getters report more bytes than the buffer holds reached a CHECK assertion in the native code behind the synchronous node:zlib APIs (deflateSync, gzipSync, brotliCompressSync, zstdCompressSync and the other synchronous zlib functions), which aborts the whole process. Node.js fixed it in 22.23.2 (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/july-2026-security-releases; commit https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/0d072480c3dbbad6db8723e39786321646989343, 'zlib: throw on out-of-bounds write buffers'), which replaces the two CHECK(Buffer::IsWithinBounds(...)) assertions in src/node_zlib.cc with an ERR_OUT_OF_RANGE error, 'input buffer is out of bounds' or 'output buffer is out of bounds'. The CVE record lists 22.x up to and including 22.23.1 as affected (https://www.cve.org/CVERecord?id=CVE-2026-58045). We checked the usr/bin/node program, the only ELF file in the nodejs-22, nodejs-22-dev and nodejs-22-doc packages, of every nodejs-22 build published in the DHI Alpine 3.23 repository by 2026-11-27 (22.22.0-r0 to 22.23.5-r0, 13 builds), on x86_64 and aarch64; both architectures agree. 22.22.0-r0 to 22.23.1-r0 still embed the assertion text Buffer::IsWithinBounds(in_off, in_len, Buffer::Length(in_buf)) and its out_off/out_buf counterpart, and contain neither new error message. 22.23.2-r0 and every later build contain both error messages and no longer contain the assertion text. Each build's node program carries the Node.js version its package version names. The range ends at 22.23.2-r0.
